# #149 feat: multiple pages in one drawing [OPEN] assignees=
closedBy=

# Issue Description

## Summary

A drawing has one canvas. Users who need several related diagrams must use separate files or put everything on one huge canvas. This feature adds pages: several canvases in one drawing.

The spec below is a starting point. The acceptance criteria are incomplete, and the open questions must be answered before implementation.

## User Story

**As a** user, **I want** several pages in one drawing **so that** I can keep related diagrams together without mixing them on one canvas.

## User Scenario

A developer makes a drawing for a system design with three pages: "Architecture," "Database," and "UI flow." She switches between them with tabs and sends the file to a teammate, who opens it with all three pages.

She sends the drawing to a teammate, who opens it and sees all three pages. The teammate can navigate between pages, make changes, and collaborate without affecting unrelated pages.

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Large
**Reason:** Pages change how a drawing is stored, edited, saved, exported, and shared in live collaboration. The feature requires changes to the underlying scene data model, page management UI, editing history, and file operations.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria (draft, incomplete)

* [ ] Users can add a page and switch between pages with tabs.
* [ ] Each page shows only its own elements.
* [ ] Saving and reopening a drawing keeps all its pages.
* [ ] A file saved before this feature opens with all its content on a single page.
* [ ] More criteria needed, based on the open questions below.

Acceptance criteria should also cover invalid input, failures, conflicts, and permissions, not only the main path.

## Open Question

* How do undo and redo work across pages?
* What happens when a page is deleted? Can it be undone? Can the last page be deleted?
* What happens if an older version of Excalidraw opens a file with pages?
* In live collaboration, what happens when someone deletes or renames the page another user is on? What do users see of collaborators on other pages?
* How do copy, paste, and export work with pages?
* Does anything get slow with many pages or many elements?

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

* Links between pages
* Presenting pages as slides
* Universal elements that appear on every page.

Note: pages are not frames. Frames group elements on the same canvas. Pages are separate canvases in the same file.

## Head Issue

This is the head issue.
Areas this touches: Scene data model and serialization, Page management and navigation UI, Page creation, deletion, duplication, and editing, Undo and redo, Saving, loading, and file compatibility, Copying, pasting, and exporting, Live collaboration and conflict resolution, Performance and reliability.


## COMMENTS

# #157 Implement Page Creation and Navigation [CLOSED] assignees=tristanraab
closedBy=178

# Issue Description

## Summary
Implement the ability to create pages within a drawing and navigate between them using a page navigation interface on right side of screen.
Display a miniature preview of each page in the navigation interface.

## User Story
**As a** user, **I want** to create and switch between pages, **so that** I can organize different diagrams within one drawing.

## User Scenario
1. User creates a drawing
2. User adds another page to the drawing
3. User can navigate between the two pages

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium
**Specific:** Greater Medium (8 points)
**Reason:** Adds page creation and navigation, while handles edge cases such as how to stop from having no pages.

Rough Scope

  - Implement the underlying page data structure and integrate it with the existing scene model.
  - Add functionality to create new pages.
  - Add page tabs or another suitable navigation interface on right side of the screen.
  - Add display thumbnail that show mini display of page for quick recogncion
  - Allow users to switch between pages.
  - Ensure each page displays only its own elements.
  - Preserve each page's contents, settings, and viewport when switching.
  - Ensure new pages receive unique internal IDs and default settings.
  - Handle invalid page creation and failures without corrupting existing pages.
  - Ensure the drawing always contains at least one page.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] **Creation:** Users can create a new page in their drawing. This page is separate from the rest of the drawing and is not affected by anything on the the other pages.
* [ ] **Navigation:** Users can navigate between two different pages. These pages display separate things and the drawing changes when the page changes.
* [ ] **Exclusivity:** Each page shows only its own content. If one object is present on one page, it isn't present on the other page.

## Open Question

N/A

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

  - Deleting Pages
  - Clearing Pages (From foundation of repo the clear button will still clear but whether it deletes all but main page, clears all page, clear first page, or clears current page is unknown).
  - Changing Pages names and adding description
  - Duplicating pages
  - Changing page order
  - Transfering elements between pages or copying element from one page to another
  - Importing or exporting multiple pages
  - saving and loading multipe pages
  - making old excalidraw drawning turn into one page whiteboard
  - adding live collab
  - page specific undo/redo

## Head Issue

Issue (#149): Multiple pages in one drawing

## Dependencies
Foundational issue for the entire feature.


## COMMENTS

# #158 Implement Page Deletion [CLOSED] assignees=tuna-fisher
closedBy=183

# Issue Description

## Summary
With the implementation of the 'pages' system, there comes an inherent need to add functionality to delete them. Without this stopgap in place, unnecessary bloat would be inevitable, and overall user control would be reduced.
Allow users to delete individual pages or multiple selected pages while protecting against accidental data loss.

## User Story
As a user, I want to delete unnecessary pages so that I can keep my workspace both clean, organized, and compact.

## User Scenario
A user creates a second page in Excalidraw. They do some work on the page, create some elements, and realize that they don't exactly need the page anymore. They then navigate to the 'delete page' button, and successfully delete the page without any data loss.
---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium
**Specific:** Lesser Medium (5 points)
**Reason:** Implement page deletion, including deleting all but current page and delete all.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] **Functionality:** Add functionality to delete pages
* [ ] **GUI:** Add a button to delete pages located within one of the menus associated with pages
* [ ] **Mass Deletion:** Add functionality to delete all pages at once
* [ ] **Customization:** Add ability to delete multiple selected pages at once
* [ ] **Ranges:** Add ability to delete a specified range of pages
* [ ] **Recreation:** Create a new blank page when all pages are deleted
* [ ] **Confirmation:** Create a 'confirmation' dialogue before a page(s) is deleted
* [ ]  **Preservation:** Preserve the data of pages for long enough to allow for sufficient opportunity to 'undo' a deletion
* [ ]  **Prevention:** Ensure that unauthorized users can't delete pages
* [ ] **Insurance** Ensure that invalid selections of page deletions can't be made

## Open Question
-How long should data be preserved for undo/redo?
-How exactly should live collaboration conflicts be handled?
-Is the latter issue within scope?
-How do we decide whether a user is authorized to delete pages or not

**Fill if in Sprint 3 Milestone**

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

  - Adding pages
  - creating page navigation
  - Clearing Pages (From foundation of repo the clear button will still clear but whether it deletes all but main page, clears all page, clear first page, or clears current page is unknown).
  - Changing Pages names and adding description
  - Duplicating pages
  - Changing page order
  - Transfering elements between pages or copying element from one page to another
  - Importing or exporting multiple pages
  - saving and loading multipe pages
  - making old excalidraw drawning turn into one page whiteboard
  - adding live collab
  - page specific undo/redo


## Head Issue

Issue (#149): Multiple pages in one drawing

## Dependencies
Issue #157

## COMMENTS
--- AntWill-08 2026-11-17:
Approved. The summary, user story, and scenario clearly establish the need for page deletion and user control. The acceptance criteria cover individual and bulk deletion, confirmation, undo protection, and safeguards against invalid or unauthorized deletions. The scope is appropriate for a Medium (5-point) issue, although the open questions around authorization, collaboration conflicts, and undo data retention should be clarified before implementation. # #159 Implement Page Clearing [CLOSED] assignees=NotaThomas
closedBy=181

# Issue Description

## Summary
Allow users to remove elements from individual pages, multiple selected pages, or all pages without deleting the pages themselves.

## User Story
**As a** user, **I want** to be able to clear pages **so that** I can get rid of mistakes that I make and remove elements that I no longer want.

## User Scenario
Developer adds the wrong diagram to one of their pages. The developer selected 'clear', which puts them in clearing mode, then selects 'clear current page', which deletes all elements on the current page. The developer then selects 'cancel' which returns them to normal mode.

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium
**Specific:** Lesser medium (5 points)
**Reason:** Clearing mode where user can select the individual pages they want to clear or mass select all pages to clear them all. Changing currently existing clear canvas functionality to work within the paradigm that the pages are sub-canvases of the main canvas. Changes to UI and underlying functionality.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] **Clearing mode:** There should be a button that says 'enter clearing mode' around/in the navigation menu. When it is pressed, it should open a menu to the side so that the user can still see the page they are on. The menu should have an augmented navigation menu that displays all the pages and indicates in some way the page the user is currently on. There should be a 'clear' option and an option to exit clearing mode.
* [ ] **Clear selection:** The user should be able to select the pages they want to clear from the augmented menu. The user should also be able to choose to select all pages. The pages they have selected should indicate that they have been selected.
* [ ] **Clearing confirmation:** When the user selects the 'clear' option while in clearing mode, the user should be prompted to confirm their choice. If the user confirms it, then pages that were selected from the augmented menu should be cleared.
* [ ] **Closing clearing mode:** The clearing options should only be visible when in clearing mode. Clearing mode should remain open until the user selects the exit option, which closes clearing mode.
* [ ] **Clearing mode across page groups:** If there are two drawings that have pages, entering clearing mode in one should not enter clearing mode in the other, and exiting clearing mode in one should not exit clearing mode in the other.
* [ ] **Clear canvas option:** There is already a clear canvas option that exists in Excalidraw. We are considering the pages to be 'sub-canvases', so the pre-existing clear canvas option should be changed to give the user the option to clear the canvas and all sub-canvases, or just the canvas.

## Open Question

* How should the pages selected to be cleared be indicated to the user? For example, should there be a checked box next to the selected pages?
* Should the user should still be able to navigate to different pages while in clearing mode?
* Should there be anything additional to indicated to the user that they are in clearing mode? For example, a banner telling the user that they are currently in clearing mode?

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

* Deleting pages
* Changing anything about the properties of pages themselves that are unrelated to the elements on the page (the page order, page names, etc.)
* Undo/redo functionality
* Creating pages
* Transferring elements from one page to another (ex. copying and pasting elements between pages)

## Head Issue

Issue (#149): Multiple pages in one drawing

## Dependencies
Issue #157

## COMMENTS
--- AntWill-08 2026-11-18:
Approved. The summary, user story, and scenario clearly establish the purpose of clearing page contents without deleting the pages themselves. The acceptance criteria cover clearing individual or multiple pages, selecting all pages, confirmation, and maintaining clearing mode independently across drawings. The scope appropriately addresses both the new clearing interface and integration with the existing clear canvas functionality. The open questions regarding selection indicators, navigation, and clearing mode visibility should be resolved before implementation to ensure a consistent user experience.
# #160 Implement Page Naming and Customization [CLOSED] assignees=AntWill-08
closedBy=184

# Issue Description

## Summary
Allow users to rename pages and customize their individual page settings.
Add descriptions or additional information to pages.

## User Story
**As a** user, **I want** to change page info **so that** I can keep pages better organized.

## User Scenario
1. The user right-click the a page tab or presses shortcut key to select current page tab
2. Opens menu with page name and meta data.
3. user clicks edit ui button to change info
4. user saves or reject changes made
5. User closes menu
6. Hovering over the tabs or reenters menu to displays the meta data.

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium
**Specific:** Lesser medium (5 points)
**Reason:** Adds user choice to change page names, add meta data such as desription of the page and customize individual page settings.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Page Information Menu and Settings
- [ ] Users can open a page information menu by right-clicking a page tab or using an available keyboard shortcut (established in PR) while a page tab is selected. Opens the intended page, even if that page is not currently active.
- [ ] The menu displays the page's unique name, description, and hide/show thumbnail option.
- [ ] Users can explicitly save or cancel changes made through the page editing interface.
- [ ] Canceling discards unsaved changes and restores the previously saved page information and settings. Closing the menu without making changes does not modify the page.
- [ ] Users can modify the supported page-specific settings (Grid). Changes to a page's settings do not unintentionally affect other pages or global application preferences. Each page retains its own customization settings when users switch between pages.

### 2. Rename Pages and Data
- [ ] Users can edit the name of an existing page through the page information menu. Users can add, edit, or remove a description for an individual page.
- [ ] New changes are reflected in the page tab and anywhere else the page name is displayed. Descriptions and Page metadata are accessible by hovering over the corresponding page tab or reopening its information menu, displaying it in a tooltip or equivalent interface.
- [ ] Long descriptions and metadata are displayed without overflowing or obstructing, and excessively long metadata won't allow saving (Max: character cap of 350)
- [ ] Page names cannot be empty or consist entirely of whitespace. Empty descriptions are permitted and do not display unnecessary empty metadata.




## Open Question

N/A

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

  - Creating Pages
  - Page navigation
  - Deleting Pages
  - Clearing Pages (From foundation of repo the clear button will still clear but whether it deletes all but main page, clears all page, clear first page, or clears current page is unknown).
  - Duplicating pages
  - Changing page order
  - Transfering elements between pages or copying element from one page to another
  - Importing or exporting multiple pages
  - saving and loading multipe pages
  - making old excalidraw drawning turn into one page whiteboard
  - adding live collab
  - page specific undo/redo

## Head Issue

Issue (#149): Multiple pages in one drawing

## Dependencies
Issue #157

## COMMENTS
--- NotaThomas 2026-11-19:
Approved. The summary, user story, and user scenario clearly establish the goal of allowing users to rename pages, add descriptions, and customize page settings without affecting other functionality such as changing page order or deleting pages. The acceptance criteria cover how the new page information can be accessed/viewed, how it can be edited, and how edits should be applied. The acceptance criteria (page information menu settings and rename pages and data) are testable. The scope accurately accesses the changes to existing functionality introduced by the name changes, and the addition of meta data such as page description and other customizable settings.

# #162 Implement Page Reordering [CLOSED] assignees=AntWill-08
closedBy=195

# Issue Description

## Summary
Allow users to change the order in which pages appear in the page navigation interface. Allow users to organize pages into folders or collapsible groups.

## User Story
**As a** user, **I want** reorder and file pages **so that** I can better organize pages

## User Scenario
1. Open page menu.
2. Hold Shift left click on page tab to drag and drop the order user prefer. User can input a number in the page tab menu to immediately move the current page to that spot.
3. Hold Shift and right-click to select a page, select multiple pages and press ui button to create folder.
4. Name folder
5. Folder moves to the end of the page menu tab list, can still be reorder like page.

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Small
**Specific:** Small (3 points)
**Reason:** Allow page order to be swapped around in tab menu.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

## **Acceptance Criteria**

 - [ ] **Criteria A: Reorder Pages:** Users can hold Shift and left-click a page tab to drag and drop it into a new position in the page navigation menu. Users can also enter a numerical position through the page tab menu to move the selected page directly to that position, with the order updating immediately.
 - [ ] **Criteria B: Create Page Folders:** Users can hold Shift and right-click page tabs to select multiple pages, then use a UI button to group the selected pages into a folder. Users must be able to assign a name to the newly created folder.
 - [ ] **Criteria C: Organize Folders:** Newly created folders appear at the end of the page navigation list and can be reordered using the same drag-and-drop interaction as individual pages. Users can expand and collapse folders to show or hide their contained pages.
 - [ ] **Criteria D: Enter number too high:** If the user inputs a number higher than the number of pages than the page will just be moved to the end.
 - [ ] **Criteria E: Enter number too low:** If the user inputs zero, then the page will just be moved to the start. (As if 1 was entered.)
 - [ ] **Criteria F: Enter invalid input** If the user inputs a negative number or something that is not a number, then the page will not move. With a quick notification that the input is invalid

# #165 Implement Multi-Page Saving and Loading [CLOSED] assignees=tristanraab
closedBy=182

# Issue Description

## Summary
Extend drawing serialization and storage to preserve multiple pages and their independent contents and settings.

## User Story
As a user, I want all pages to be saved within one drawing so that I can reopen the drawing without losing any of my diagrams.

## User Scenario
1. User creates a drawing
2. User creates a page within this drawing
3. User saves the drawing and the page is still present

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Small
**Specific:** Small (3 points)
**Reason:** Reworks the save and export to account for multiple pages implementation

Rough Scope

  - Update the drawing data structure to store multiple pages.
  - Store each page's elements, settings, and other required state.
  - Preserve page order and the active page.
  - Ensure all pages are serialized and deserialized correctly.
  - Ensure inactive pages are not accidentally discarded.
  - Handle corrupted or incomplete page data.
  - Handle duplicate page IDs and invalid references.
  - Preserve the existing single-page file format behavior where possible.
  - Ensure saving failures do not silently lose unsaved work.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] **Persistence:** Pages persist when the drawing is saved. When the drawing is reopened, the pages are still present.
* [ ] **Multiple Pages:** If there are multiple pages, they all are saved in the drawing.

## Open Question

N/A

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

- Creating pages
- Deleting pages
- Clearing pages
- Collaboration on pages
- Changing Pages names and adding description
- Duplicating pages
- Changing page order
- Transfering elements between pages or copying element from one page to another

## Head Issue

Issue (#149): Multiple pages in one drawing

## Dependencies
Issue (#157). This is a foundational technical requirement and should be developed alongside the initial page implementation rather than postponed until the end.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|:---:|---|
| Correctness —<br>does the change do what the issue asked? | 4 | Both ACs work in the simple case,<br>but there are 3 bugs (below), including<br>lost drawings after a reload. |
| Test coverage —<br>are tests present and meaningful? | 2 | No automated tests were added. |
| Code quality —<br>consistent style, clear naming,<br>no unnecessary duplication | 5 | Style matches, but the restore in<br>`syncActionResult` runs on every action,<br>and `pages` stays in `this.state` (bug 1). |
| Documentation —<br>inline comments and PR description are clear | 5 | "What changed" is cut off.<br>The new restore branch has no comments. |
| AI transparency —<br>if AI was used, is there evidence<br>of human verification? | 4 | The Copilot log is in `ai-logs/`, but the PR<br>has no AI Usage section or link to it. |
| Test evidence —<br>does every AC have a test?<br>Are the expected values justified?<br>Which tests did you run locally? | 3 | No AC has an automated test.<br>Expected values come from the ACs.<br>Ran locally: typecheck, ESLint, Prettier,<br>and the existing page/export/data tests<br>(94 passed, none cover the new code).<br>Bugs reproduced by hand. |

**Bugs**

1. **Drawings are lost after a reload.** Steps: create a second page, reload, draw a rectangle, click zoom in (+). The rectangle disappears, the zoom doesn't change, and the loss is saved. Cause: on load, `syncActionResult` spreads `sceneActionResult.appState` into state, so `pages` stays in `this.state`. Most actions return `{...appState, ...}`, so every later action re-enters the restore branch with that stale snapshot and replaces the scene with it. The restore should only run when a scene is loaded, and `pages` shouldn't stay in state.
2. **Hidden collaborators' drawings leak into saved files.** `prepareDataForJSONExport` filters the top-level elements with `getLocallyVisibleElements` (#116), but `appState.pages` holds the active page's full element list from `getElementsIncludingDeleted()`. I hid a collaborator and saved: their element was missing from `elements` but present in `appState.pages`, and reopening the file restores from `pages`, so it comes back. The pages need the same filtering as the exported elements.
3. **Opening an older single-page file keeps the previous drawing's pages.** With two pages open, I opened a file without `pages`: it replaced the active page, but the other page stayed, and the next save writes it into that file. #165's scope says to preserve the single-page format, so loading a file without pages should reset to a single page.

**Tests to add:** a save → load round trip with two pages, an action after a reload (bug 1), a hidden collaborator on save (bug 2), and loading an older file without `pages` (bug 3).

23	## Why
24
25	Issue #158 (child of #149, depends on #157). #157 added multiple pages to a drawing, but once a page existed there was no way to get rid of it. This PR adds a **deleting mode** to the Pages sidebar, next to #159's clearing mode. You select one, several (including a range!) or all pages and delete them after a confirmation. Deleting every page leaves one new blank page.
26
27	Deleting mode is built as an extension of #159's clearing mode. Both modes share the same page selection (checkboxes, Select all, the new **All but current** button and the new **select by number** field). They differ only in the final action: **Clear** empties the selected pages, while **Delete** removes them. Other page actions could become further modes later on the same pattern.
28
29	How this PR answers the issue's open questions:
30	- **How long should data be preserved for undo/redo?** Data isn't preserved. Undoing a deletion is out of scope (see Tech Debt). Every page switch, including creating a page, already clears the shared undo history (#157), so restoring a deleted page would need page-specific undo/redo, which the other page issues also list as out of scope. The confirmation dialog guards against accidental deletion instead, and says "This can't be undone."
31	- **How should live collaboration conflicts be handled? Is that in scope?** Out of scope. Pages aren't synced to collaborators yet.
32	- **How do we decide whether a user may delete pages?** For now, deleting is blocked in view mode, the same way #157 blocks adding pages. Real permissions can come in a later issue.
33
34	## What changed
35
36	- **Deletion logic (`pages.ts`):**
37	  - `deletePages(pages, pageIds, activePageId, generateId)` returns the remaining pages and the new active page. If the active page is deleted, the closest remaining page before it becomes active, or the first one after it. Deleting every page returns one new blank page. It throws on an empty selection or an unknown page id. Pages are kept or dropped as they are, never rebuilt field by field, so fields other issues add (for example #160's names) survive.
38	  - `parsePageRange(input, pages)` turns 1-based positions like `2-4, 7` into page ids in page order. It returns `null` for empty input, non-numbers, `0`, positions past the last page, reversed ranges (`4-2`) and stray commas.
39	  - `getPageLabel(page, index)` is now the one place page labels ("Page 3") are built, so #160 only has to change this function to show page names.
40	- **Deleting pages (`App.tsx`):**
41	  - Private `deletePages(pageIds)`. It does nothing in view mode. If the active page survives, the canvas and its undo history are left alone and only the page list re-renders. If the active page is deleted, it switches to the new active page the same way `selectPage` does: undo history is cleared, so undo can't replay a deleted page's edits on another page.
42	  - Private `pageSelectionMode: "clear" | "delete"`, plus `enterPageDeletingMode()` and `deleteSelectedPages()`, modelled on #159's clearing methods. It's an App field rather than an `AppState` field, so no snapshot files change. The only edit to #159's code is one line in `enterPageClearingMode()`, which sets the mode back to `"clear"`.
43	  - Private `setPageSelection(pageIds)` replaces the selection of whichever mode is on. Both "All but current" and the range field use it.
44	- **Deleting-mode UI (`Pages.tsx`, `Pages.scss`, `LayerUI.tsx`):**
45	  - Normal mode: an **Enter deleting mode** button under **Enter clearing mode**. It's disabled in view mode.
46	  - Deleting mode reuses #159's checkbox page list and adds a "Deleting mode: select pages to delete" header, a red **Delete** button (disabled until something is ticked, and in view mode) and **Exit deleting mode**. Like clearing mode, you stay in the mode after deleting, with the checkboxes reset.
47	  - Both modes now share four rows of controls:
48	    ```
49	    [ Select all pages ][ All but current ]
50	    [ e.g. 2-4, 7                ][ Select ]
51	    [ Delete ]  /  [ Clear ]
52	    [ Exit deleting mode ]  /  [ Exit clearing mode ]
53	    ```
54	  - **All but current** selects every page except the one you're on, replacing the current selection. It's disabled when there's only one page.
55	- **Confirmation (`PageDeleteDialog.tsx`):** a new dialog built on the existing `ConfirmDialog`. It lists the pages being deleted ("This will delete Page 1, Page 3 and everything on them. This can't be undone.") and, when every page is selected, adds "A new blank page will be created in their place."
56	- **Select by number (`PageRangeSelect.tsx`):**
57	  - A field plus a **Select** button. Valid input, by button or Enter, replaces the selection and empties the field.
58	  - Invalid input disables Select, marks the field invalid and shows "Enter page numbers from 1 to N, like 2-4, 7" under it. A field holding only spaces counts as empty.
59	  - The field's accessible name comes from `aria-label`, and the error is linked with `aria-describedby`.
60	- **Strings (`en.json`):** `labels.deletingMode`, `labels.selectPageRange`, `labels.pageRangePlaceholder`; `buttons.enterDeletingMode`, `exitDeletingMode`, `selectOtherPages`, `selectPageRange`; `errors.invalidPageRange`; `deletePagesDialog.title`, `message`, `allPagesNote`.
61	- **Mutation testing (sprint 3 D6):**
62	  - StrykerJS 9.6.1 with the Vitest runner, reusing NotaThomas's #159 setup. It's run with `yarn test:mutation stryker.158.config.mjs` (`stryker.158.config.mjs`, `vitest.stryker.158.config.mts`).
63	  - The config works out the lines to mutate from `git diff` against the branch's fork point from master.
64	  - The reports and the write-up are in `docs/sprint3/mutation/`. The score went from 91.98% to 96.23%; details under Test Evidence.

66	## Tech Debt
67
68	### Introduced
69
70	- **Deleting pages can't be undone.** The issue's "Preservation" criterion was moved to Out of Scope (see Why).
71	- **View mode is the only lock on deleting** (marked with a `shortcut:` comment in `App.deletePages`). There's no real permission model yet.
72	- **`pageClearingSelection` now holds the selection for both modes.** I kept #159's name and added a comment rather than renaming merged code. A rename to something like `pageSelection` would read better if more modes are added.
73	- **Page labels are positions** ("Page 3" becomes "Page 2" when an earlier page is deleted). This comes from #157. `getPageLabel` is where #160 can switch to page names.
74	- **The range field forgets what you typed** after selecting, because positions shift once pages are deleted.
75	- **New strings are in `en.json` only.**
76	- **`deletePages` is private on `App`** and not part of `excalidrawAPI`, so host apps can't delete pages programmatically.

192	## Why
193
194	Issue #159 (child of #149, depends on #157). #157 added multiple pages to a drawing, but there was no way to remove the elements on a page except deleting them by hand. Excalidraw's existing "Clear canvas" option also didn't know about pages. This issue adds a **clearing mode** to the Pages sidebar: you select one, several or all pages and clear them after a confirmation, and the pages themselves are kept. It also changes "Clear canvas" so that, with more than one page, you can clear just the page you're on (the canvas) or that page and every other page (its sub-canvases).
195
196	How this PR answers the issue's open questions:
197	- **How are selected pages shown?** Each page gets a checkbox with a check mark and a red border when selected.
198	- **Can you navigate between pages in clearing mode?** No. Clicking a page selects or deselects it. Exit clearing mode to navigate.
199	- **Is there an extra indicator for clearing mode?** Yes, a red "Clearing mode: select pages to clear" header above the page list.
200
201	While testing with many pages, the page list turned out not to scroll: pages past the bottom of the window were cut off. This PR fixes that too.
202
203	## What changed
204
205	- **Clearing-mode state (`types.ts`, `appState.ts`):** a new `AppState.pageClearingSelection: readonly string[] | null`. `null` means clearing mode is off; otherwise it holds the ids of the selected pages. It lives in each editor's own state, so two drawings on one page don't affect each other. It is never saved to local storage, exports or the server.
206	- **Clearing pages (`App.tsx`):**
207	  - New public methods `getPageIds()`, `getActivePageId()` and `clearPages(pageIds)`, also added to `AppClassProperties`.
208	  - `clearPages` empties pages that aren't open by setting their stored `elements` to `[]`. For the page you're on, it marks its elements deleted through `updateScene`, so that clear can be undone, and resets the selection.
209	  - Pages keep their settings (background, scroll, grid). Image files aren't removed, because other pages may still use them.
210	  - Private handlers for entering and exiting clearing mode, toggling a page, selecting or deselecting all, and clearing the selection. After a clear, clearing mode stays on and the selection resets.
211	- **Clearing-mode UI (`Pages.tsx`, `Pages.scss`, `LayerUI.tsx`):**
212	  - Normal mode: an **Enter clearing mode** button under **+ Add page**. Both are disabled in view mode.
213	  - Clearing mode:
214	    - Each page becomes a checkbox (`role="checkbox"`, `aria-checked`). The page you're on gets a "Current" badge and `aria-current="page"`.
215	    - Buttons: **Select all pages / Deselect all pages**, **Clear** (disabled until something is selected), and **Exit clearing mode**. **Add page** is hidden.
216	    - **Clear** opens a confirmation stating how many pages will be cleared. Its state is local to the component, so it's per editor, and it's dropped whenever clearing mode turns on or off.
217	- **Seeing the page while clearing (`DefaultSidebar.tsx`):** while clearing mode is on and the Pages tab is open, the sidebar is forced to dock, the same way the search tab already is. The canvas shrinks beside the menu instead of being covered, and clicking the canvas doesn't close the menu. Closing the sidebar doesn't end clearing mode; reopening it shows clearing mode again.
218	- **Clear canvas (`actionCanvas.tsx`, `ActiveConfirmDialog.tsx`, `ConfirmDialog.tsx`):**
219	  - `actionClearCanvas` takes `{ scope?: "canvas" | "allPages" }`. With `"allPages"`, it calls `clearPages` on every other page, then clears the current page as before. It also no longer exits clearing mode.
220	  - With more than one page, the dialog (main menu, Ctrl+Delete, command palette) offers **Clear this canvas only** and **Clear canvas and all pages**. With one page it's unchanged.
221	  - `ConfirmDialog` takes an optional second confirm button (`onSecondaryConfirm`, `secondaryConfirmText`). The shared close-and-refocus logic moved into a `runAndRefocus` helper.
222	- **Scrollable page list (`Pages.scss`, `LayerUI.tsx`):** the page list now scrolls inside the sidebar, and the buttons stay pinned below it. The sidebar's flex layout had no `min-height: 0`, so the list grew past the window and the sidebar clipped it. The fix is scoped to the Pages tab (`.page-navigation-tab` and a `:has()` rule on the tabs root), so Library and Search are unchanged.
223	- **Strings (`en.json`):** `labels.currentPage`, `labels.clearingMode`; `buttons.enterClearingMode`, `exitClearingMode`, `clearPages`, `selectAllPages`, `deselectAllPages`, `clearCanvasOnly`, `clearCanvasAndPages`; `clearCanvasDialog.withPages`; `clearPagesDialog.title`, `clearPagesDialog.content`.
224	- **Snapshots:** four snapshot files gain `"pageClearingSelection": null` and nothing else.
225	- **Mutation testing (sprint 3):**
226	  - StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Vitest runner, run with `yarn test:mutation` (`stryker.config.mjs`, `vitest.stryker.config.mts`).
227	  - Reports and the write-up are in `docs/sprint3/mutation/`. The score went from 69.67% to 90.40%; details under Test Evidence.

229	## Tech Debt
230
231	### Introduced
232
233	- **Only the current page's clear can be undone.** Undo history only tracks the open page, so pages that weren't open when you cleared them can't be restored. Undo/redo was out of scope for this issue.
234	- **No navigation in clearing mode:** clicking a page selects it instead of opening it. You have to exit clearing mode to switch pages.
235	- **The docked sidebar can't be undocked during clearing mode.** On narrow screens the docked sidebar takes a big share of the width.
236	- **New strings are in `en.json` only.**
237	- **`clearPages`, `getPageIds` and `getActivePageId` are public on `App`** but not part of `excalidrawAPI`, so host apps can't clear pages programmatically yet.
238
239	### Encountered
240
241	- **The confirm dialog's state is shared between editors.** `activeConfirmDialogAtom` lives in `editorJotaiStore`, which is created once per module, so every editor on the page shares it: Ctrl+Delete in one drawing opens the Clear canvas dialog in all of them. Clearing mode avoids this by keeping its state in `AppState` and component state. The page tests reset the atom in `beforeEach`, because a dialog left open by one test otherwise leaked into the next.
242	- **Pages are still in memory only (from #157):** they aren't saved, exported or synced to collaborators, so cleared or uncleared pages other than the current one are lost on reload.
243	- **The default sidebar's flex layout can't scroll long content:** no `min-height: 0` anywhere in the chain. This PR only fixes it for the Pages tab.
244	- **Excalidraw's undo can't restore elements that were added outside history** (for example via `updateScene` without `CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY`). One test had to add its element in its own history step.
245	- **Test failures not caused by this PR:**
246	  - `scene/__snapshots__/export.test.ts.snap` has 1 obsolete snapshot from an earlier pages commit. It was left alone.

314	--- NotaThomas:
315	## Design Decision
316
317	Field | Description
318	-- | --
319	Decision | When in clearing mode, the user can't switch to a different page. Pressing on a page selects the page to be cleared instead of instead of bringing the user to that page.
320	Alternatives considered | 1. Allow the user to switch pages while in clearing mode, and have a different button near the pages to select them to be cleared. 2. Have a different UI element where the user could select pages to be cleared, instead of extending the already existing page navigation menu.
321	Rationale | I chose to extend the currently existing page navigation menu as it was simpler than adding a completely new element and helps to reduce visual clutter. Also, it seems a bit more intuitive than having the selector to clear pages being an entirely different menu. I chose to not let users be able to switch to different pages while in clearing mode since they might accidentally switch to a page when attempting to select it to be cleared, which could be annoying.  Not allowing users to switch pages allowed me to extend the pre-existing navigation menu as much as possible since I had to add fewer extra buttons than alternative 1.
322	Consequences | If a user to trying to mass clear pages and they want to view each of them as they select them to be cleared, they will not be able to do so and remain in clearing mode, which would make the process of viewing and clearing all those pages take longer (since they would have to enter clearing mode, clear the page, exit clearing mode, switch pages, then repeat). However, a user will also not be able to accidentally switch pages while attempting to clear pages, which could save the user some annoyance.

24	## Why
25
26	Issue #160 (child of #149, depends on #157). After #157, pages could be created and switched, but each one was only "Page N" based on its position, with no way to tell pages apart or note what they're for. This sub-issue adds a page info menu so users can rename pages, add a description, hide or show a page's thumbnail and set each page's own grid. Pages become easier to organize, and the info can be read by hovering a tab.
27
28	## What changed
29
30	- **Data model (`packages/excalidraw/pages.ts`):** `DrawingPage` gains:
31	  - `name: string`: new pages get the first free "Page N" name, so default names never repeat.
32	  - `description: string`: empty by default.
33	  - `showThumbnail: boolean`: `true` by default.
34	- **Validation helpers (`pages.ts`):** `validatePageInfo` and `isPageInfoValid`, the single source for the rules:
35	  - Names can't be empty or whitespace only.
36	  - Names must be unique (trimmed, ignoring case).
37	  - Names are at most 50 characters (`PAGE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`).
38	  - Descriptions are at most 350 characters (`PAGE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH`).
39	  - `getNextDefaultPageName` generates the default names.
40	- **Page info menu (new `PageInfoDialog.tsx` / `.scss`):**
41	  - It opens in a read-only view showing the name, the description (only when there is one), thumbnail shown/hidden and a grid summary.
42	  - **Edit** switches to a form with: name, description (with an `n/350` counter), show thumbnail, show grid, snap to grid and grid size.
43	  - Inline errors explain why a page can't be saved, and **Save** stays disabled until everything is valid.
44	  - **Cancel** throws away the edits. **Close**, Escape or clicking outside closes without changing anything.
45	- **Opening the menu:**
46	  - Right-click a page tab, or press **F2** on a focused tab. Both open *that* page's menu without switching to it.
47	  - **Alt+Shift+I** (new `actionOpenPageInfo`) opens the menu for the current page from anywhere.
48	  - Both shortcuts are listed in the Help dialog.
49	- **Page tabs (`Pages.tsx`):**
50	  - Tabs show the page's name (also used as the accessible name), cut off with "…" when too long.
51	  - Hovering a tab shows its description in a tooltip. Pages without a description get no tooltip.
52	  - Hiding the thumbnail replaces the preview with a small page icon and skips rendering the preview.
53	- **Per-page grid (`App.tsx` `updatePageInfo`):**
54	  - Grid changes for a page that isn't open are stored on that page only. The current page and other pages are untouched.
55	  - Grid changes for the open page apply right away.
56	  - Turning the grid on at opacity 0 restores full opacity, the same as the existing Ctrl+' toggle.
57	  - `updatePageInfo` re-checks and trims the name itself, so code that skips the UI still can't save an invalid name.
58	- **Keyboard handling:** other shortcuts are ignored while the menu is open, so typing in it can't trigger tools.
59	- **i18n:** new `pageInfoDialog` section and `labels.pageInfo` in `en.json`.
60
61	## Tech Debt
62
63	### Introduced
64
65	- **Not saved yet.** Names, descriptions and thumbnail settings live in `App`'s private page list, like the rest of #157's page data, so they're lost on reload. Saving and loading pages is out of scope for this issue.
66	- **Default names keep their original language.** "Page N" is filled in from `t("labels.page")` when the page is created, so it doesn't follow a later language change.
67	- **The 50-character name limit is my choice.** The issue only sets a limit for descriptions (350).
68	- **Changes can't be undone.** Edits made through the page info menu don't go into undo history. Page-specific undo/redo is out of scope.
69	- **The shortcut matches the physical I key.** Alt+Shift+I checks `event.code === "KeyI"` so it works with Option on macOS. On non-QWERTY layouts it's whichever key sits where I is on QWERTY.
70	- **Leftovers:**
71	  - `getPageForInfo` (on `AppClassProperties`) isn't used by the UI, since `LayerUI` looks the page up itself.
72	  - The `page-navigation__item--no-thumbnail` class has no CSS rule yet.
73	- **Long descriptions make a tall tooltip.** A 350-character description shows as a 50ch-wide tooltip of about 7–8 lines.
74	- New UI strings were added to `en.json` only.
75
76	### Encountered
77
78	- **Pages aren't React state.** They're private fields on `App` (from #157), so changing them doesn't re-render. `updatePageInfo` relies on its `setState` call to refresh the tabs.
79	- **The current page's settings live in two places.** They're in `this.state` and get copied into the page by `saveActivePage()`. So grid edits for the current page must go through `setState`, or they'd be overwritten on the next page switch.
80	- **Vitest also picks up the stray `.tmp-ai-logs-wt/` checkout.** The full suite runs twice (about 30 min), font fetches fail, and failures appear that aren't real.
81	- **`yarn fix` fails** with an `@typescript-eslint` plugin conflict from the nested `excalidraw-room` config. ESLint and Prettier were run on the changed files directly instead.
82	- **Some tests fail only under full-suite load:** `collabLock`, `actionDuplicateSelection` and `maskGroup` pass when run on their own. The 20K-element `fractionalIndex` performance test fails independently of this change.
83	- **`yarn test:update` deleted the "with a CJK font 2" export snapshot** while font fetches were failing. That change was reverted.

162	Closes #162
163
164	## Why
165
166	Issue #162 (child of #149, depends on #157). After #157, pages showed up in the page navigation in the order they were created, with no way to move them or group related pages. This sub-issue lets users reorder pages by Shift + dragging or by typing a position in the page menu. It also lets them group pages into named folders that can be collapsed, expanded and reordered like pages, so drawings with many pages are easier to organize.
167
168	## What changed
169
170	- **Data model (`packages/excalidraw/pages.ts`):** new `PageTree` type, the list the page navigation shows from top to bottom:
171	  - Each entry is either a page or a `PageFolder` (`id`, `name`, `collapsed`, `pageIds`).
172	  - Folders hold pages only. They never hold other folders.
173	  - Reading the tree from top to bottom, including the pages inside folders, gives the order of `App`'s page list (`getPageOrder` / `orderPages`).
174	- **Tree helpers (`pages.ts`):** these functions never change the tree they're given; each returns a new one:
175	  - `createPageTree`, `syncPageTree`: build the tree and keep it in step with the page list. New pages go at the end, and deleted pages and any folders they leave empty are removed.
176	  - `parsePagePosition`: accepts whole numbers of 0 or more. Negatives, decimals, text and empty input are rejected.
177	  - `getPagePosition`, `movePageToPosition`: read or set a page's 1-based position in its own list, which is either the top level (where a folder takes one slot) or the folder the page is in. 0 moves the page to the start, and numbers past the end move it to the end.
178	  - `moveNavItem`: drops a page or folder before or after another item. Pages can be dragged into and out of folders. Folders stay at the top level, and folders left empty are removed.
179	  - `createPageFolder`: groups the selected pages, in their current order, into a new expanded folder at the end of the list. Pages leave any folder they were in.
180	  - `deletePageFolder`, `removePageFromFolder`, `togglePageFolder`.
181	- **Page navigation (`Pages.tsx` / `.scss`):**
182	  - **Shift + drag** a page tab or folder header to reorder it. A line shows where it will land. Escape cancels the drag, and Shift + click never switches pages.
183	  - **Shift + right-click** page tabs to select them for a folder, instead of opening the page menu. A form then shows the selected count and a name field (the default name is "Folder N") with **Create folder** and **Cancel**. Create folder stays disabled while the name is empty.
184	  - Folder headers show a ▸/▾ arrow, the folder's name and its page count. Clicking a header collapses or expands the folder. A **×** button deletes the folder but keeps its pages in the folder's place.
185	  - A hint under the list explains the Shift shortcuts.
186	  - Reordering and folders are turned off in view mode and in the #158/#159 clearing and deleting modes.
187	- **Page info menu (`PageInfoDialog.tsx` / `.scss`):**
188	  - Shows the page's position ("2 of 5") and has a **Move to position** field with a **Move** button.
189	  - An invalid input (negative, not a number or empty) shows a toast ("Invalid position. Enter a whole number of 0 or more.") and the page doesn't move.
190	  - Pages inside a folder get a **Remove from folder** button, which puts the page right after its folder.
191	- **App (`App.tsx`):**
192	  - New private `pageTree` field.
193	  - `applyPageTree` reorders `pages` to match the tree and re-renders. It doesn't touch the scene, the current page or undo history.
194	  - `createPage` and `deletePages` call `syncPageTree`.
195	  - New methods: `movePageToPosition`, `getPagePosition`, `isPageInFolder`, `removePageFromFolder`. The last three are added to `AppClassProperties` along with `movePageToPosition`.
196	  - Every action that changes the order or folders is ignored in view mode, except collapsing and expanding a folder.
197	- **i18n:** new strings in `en.json` for folders, position and the invalid-position error.
198
199	## Tech Debt
200
201	### Introduced
202
203	- **Not saved yet.** Page order and folders live in `App`'s private `pageTree`, like the rest of #157's page data, so they're lost on reload. Saving and loading pages is out of scope for this issue.
204	- **Changes can't be undone.** Reordering and folder changes don't go into undo history. Page-specific undo/redo is out of scope.
205	- **Typed positions are relative to the page's own list.** A page in a folder can only be moved within that folder by number, and at the top level a folder counts as one slot. Moving a page into or out of a folder is done by dragging or with **Remove from folder**. The issue doesn't say how numbers and folders should work together, so this is my choice.
206	- **Things the issue didn't ask for:** a delete-folder button (×) and **Remove from folder** in the page menu. Without them, a folder could only be undone by dragging every page out of it.
207	- **Folders can't be renamed and names don't have to be unique.** The name is set only when the folder is created. The default "Folder N" counts the current folders, so after a folder is deleted the next default name can repeat an existing one.
208	- **Reordering needs a mouse or pointer.** No keyboard shortcut moves tabs, but keyboard users can still use Move to position in the page menu.
209	- **`pageTree` and `pages` must stay in step.** Any future code that adds or removes pages has to call `syncPageTree`. If it doesn't, `orderPages` throws on the next reorder.
210	- New UI strings were added to `en.json` only.
211
212	### Encountered
213
214	- **Pages aren't React state.** They're private fields on `App` (from #157), so changing them doesn't re-render. `applyPageTree` calls `triggerRender()` to refresh the list.
215	- **Mutation testing (Stryker) took too long.** The #162 run (`stryker.162.config.mjs`) was stopped before it finished, so no mutation score is included in this PR.
216	- [add any other issues you ran into]

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { getDefaultAppState } from "./appState";
import { t } from "./i18n";

import type { AppState } from "./types";

export type PageSettings = Pick<
  AppState,
  | "viewBackgroundColor"
  | "scrollX"
  | "scrollY"
  | "zoom"
  | "gridSize"
  | "gridStep"
  | "gridScale"
  | "gridSnapLinked"
  | "gridSnapScale"
  | "gridColor"
  | "gridOpacity"
  | "gridLayer"
  | "gridModeEnabled"
  | "gridSnapEnabled"
  | "frameRendering"
>;

export type DrawingPage = Readonly<{
  id: string;
  name: string;
  description: string;
  showThumbnail: boolean;
  elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[];
  settings: PageSettings;
}>;

export const PAGE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH = 50;
export const PAGE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH = 350;

export type PageGridSettings = Pick<
  PageSettings,
  "gridModeEnabled" | "gridSnapEnabled" | "gridSize"
>;

export type PageInfoPatch = {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  showThumbnail: boolean;
  grid: PageGridSettings;
};

export type PageInfoValidation = {
  nameError?: "empty" | "duplicate" | "tooLong";
  descriptionError?: "tooLong";
};

const normalizePageName = (name: string) => name.trim().toLocaleLowerCase();

/**
 * Returns `${baseName} N` using the smallest N >= 1 whose name isn't already
 * taken (case-insensitively) by another page.
 */
export const getNextDefaultPageName = (
  pages: readonly Pick<DrawingPage, "name">[],
  baseName: string,
): string => {
  const taken = new Set(pages.map((page) => normalizePageName(page.name)));
  let index = 1;
  while (taken.has(normalizePageName(`${baseName} ${index}`))) {
    index++;
  }
  return `${baseName} ${index}`;
};

export const validatePageInfo = (
  info: { name: string; description: string },
  pages: readonly Pick<DrawingPage, "id" | "name">[],
  pageId: string,
): PageInfoValidation => {
  const result: PageInfoValidation = {};
  const trimmedName = info.name.trim();

  if (!trimmedName) {
    result.nameError = "empty";
  } else if (trimmedName.length > PAGE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH) {
    result.nameError = "tooLong";
  } else if (
    pages.some(
      (page) =>
        page.id !== pageId &&
        normalizePageName(page.name) === normalizePageName(trimmedName),
    )
  ) {
    result.nameError = "duplicate";
  }

  if (info.description.length > PAGE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH) {
    result.descriptionError = "tooLong";
  }

  return result;
};

export const isPageInfoValid = (validation: PageInfoValidation) =>
  !validation.nameError && !validation.descriptionError;

export const getPageSettings = (appState: PageSettings): PageSettings => ({
  viewBackgroundColor: appState.viewBackgroundColor,
  scrollX: appState.scrollX,
  scrollY: appState.scrollY,
  zoom: appState.zoom,
  gridSize: appState.gridSize,
  gridStep: appState.gridStep,
  gridScale: appState.gridScale,
  gridSnapLinked: appState.gridSnapLinked,
  gridSnapScale: appState.gridSnapScale,
  gridColor: appState.gridColor,
  gridOpacity: appState.gridOpacity,
  gridLayer: appState.gridLayer,
  gridModeEnabled: appState.gridModeEnabled,
  gridSnapEnabled: appState.gridSnapEnabled,
  frameRendering: appState.frameRendering,
});

export const createPage = (id: string, name: string): DrawingPage => ({
  id,
  name,
  description: "",
  showThumbnail: true,
  elements: [],
  settings: getPageSettings(getDefaultAppState()),
});

/** The label shown for a page: its user-editable name (#160). */
export const getPageLabel = (page: DrawingPage) => page.name;

/**
 * Removes the given pages. If the active page is removed, the closest
 * surviving page before it becomes active (or the first one after it).
 * Removing every page leaves a single fresh blank page.
 */
export const deletePages = (
  pages: readonly DrawingPage[],
  pageIds: readonly string[],
  activePageId: string,
  generateId: () => string,
): { pages: readonly DrawingPage[]; activePageId: string } => {
  const toDelete = new Set(pageIds);
  if (!toDelete.size) {
    throw new Error("No pages selected for deletion");
  }

  private saveActivePage = () => {
    const activePage = this.pages.find((page) => page.id === this.activePageId);
    if (!activePage) {
      throw new Error(`Active page ${this.activePageId} does not exist`);
    }

    this.pages = this.pages.map((page) =>
      page.id === this.activePageId
        ? {
            ...page,
            elements: this.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted(),
            settings: getPageSettings(this.state),

    );

  private getPagesForUI = (): readonly DrawingPage[] => {
    const elements = this.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted();
    const settings = getPageSettings(this.state);
    return this.pages.map((page) =>
      page.id === this.activePageId ? { ...page, elements, settings } : page,
    );

  public getPagesForPersistence = (): readonly DrawingPage[] => {

  public getActivePageId = (): string => this.activePageId;

  private selectPage = (pageId: string) => {
    const page = this.pages.find((candidate) => candidate.id === pageId);
    if (!page) {
      throw new Error(`Cannot select unknown page ${pageId}`);
    }
    if (pageId === this.activePageId) {
      return;
    }

    this.saveActivePage();
    this.activePageId = pageId;
    this.history.clear();
    this.updateScene({
      elements: page.elements,
      appState: getPageActivationAppState(page.settings),
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });
  };

  public getPageForInfo = (pageId: string): DrawingPage | null =>

  public openPageInfo = (pageId: string) => {
    if (!this.pages.some((page) => page.id === pageId)) {
      return;
    }
    this.setState({ openDialog: { name: "pageInfo", pageId } });
  };

  public updatePageInfo = (pageId: string, patch: PageInfoPatch) => {
    const target = this.pages.find((page) => page.id === pageId);
    if (!target) {
      return;
    }

    const name = patch.name.trim();
    const validation = validatePageInfo(
      { name, description: patch.description },
      this.pages,
      pageId,
    );
    if (!isPageInfoValid(validation)) {
      return;
    }

    const isActive = pageId === this.activePageId;
    const currentSettings = isActive
      ? getPageSettings(this.state)
      : target.settings;
    const gridSettings = {
      ...patch.grid,
      // opacity 0 hid the grid, so showing it again starts fully visible
      gridOpacity:
        patch.grid.gridModeEnabled && currentSettings.gridOpacity === 0
          ? DEFAULT_GRID_OPACITY
          : currentSettings.gridOpacity,
    };

    this.pages = this.pages.map((page) =>
      page.id === pageId
        ? {
            ...page,
            name,
            description: patch.description,
            showThumbnail: patch.showThumbnail,
            // the active page's settings live in this.state and are written
            // back by saveActivePage(), so only inactive pages update here
            settings: isActive
              ? page.settings
              : { ...page.settings, ...gridSettings },
          }
        : page,
    );

    if (isActive) {
      this.setState({ ...gridSettings, openDialog: null });
    } else {
      this.setState({ openDialog: null });
    }
  };

import { CREATOR_ID_KEY } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

/**
 * Elements this client introduced to the room that don't carry its creator
 * stamp yet: newly drawn, pasted or duplicated (new id, possibly with a
 * copied foreign stamp), or restored by undo/redo without the stamp.
 *
 * Elements first received from other clients are never (re)stamped, so edits
 * never transfer ownership.
 *
 * @param remoteElementIds ids of elements that first reached this client from
 * the room (other clients or the room's stored scene)
 */
export const getElementsToStamp = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  remoteElementIds: ReadonlySet<string>,
  clientId: string,
): T[] =>
  elements.filter(
    (element) =>
      !element.isDeleted &&
      !remoteElementIds.has(element.id) &&
      element.customData?.[CREATOR_ID_KEY] !== clientId,
  );

export const getStampedCustomData = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  clientId: string,
): NonNullable<ExcalidrawElement["customData"]> => ({
  ...element.customData,
  [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: clientId,
});

I read everything before writing these questions: #149 (with the instructor's comment), #167, the merged sub-issues (#157, #158, #159, #160, #162, #165), their PRs (#178, #183, #181, #184, #195, #182) with reviews and design-decision comments, and the page and collab code on `master`.

## What's on master today (sets up the questions)

- **Pages aren't part of the shared scene.** They live in private fields in `App.tsx` (`pages`, `activePageId`, `pageTree`). Only the open page's elements are in the scene. Switching pages swaps them in and out and clears undo history.
- **Collaboration doesn't know about pages.** `Collab.tsx` and `Portal.tsx` broadcast and reconcile only the scene's elements, which means the open page. Firebase stores a flat list of elements with no page list, names, or order.
- **What this means (from reading the code; I haven't reproduced it in a browser yet):**
  - When user A switches to Page 2, those elements get broadcast, and user B merges them into whatever page B is on, so pages bleed into each other.
  - Page names, order, and folders never reach peers.
  - So pages and collab aren't just "not connected yet": using both together corrupts drawings today.
- **Past decisions the team made that #167 has to respect:**
  - Page names must be unique (#160, design decision).
  - Deleting the open page moves you to the closest page before it (#158).
  - View mode is the only "permission" so far (#158).
  - Page deletion can't be undone (#158).
  - Clearing pages you aren't on sets their `elements` to `[]` instead of marking them deleted (#159).
  - Hidden collaborators' elements are filtered out of saved pages (your review of #182).
- **#158's PR described collab conflicts as "out of scope, pages aren't synced yet,"** and every other sub-issue did the same. So #167 is where those questions finally get answered.

## Questions

Each one lists what follows from each answer. I've marked my pick with **(lean)** so you can just reply "agree" where you do.

### A. What gets shared

1. **Should everyone in a room see the same set of pages?** That covers the page list, names, and descriptions.
   - Yes **(lean)**. This is what "shared drawing" means in the Summary. It needs a new message for page metadata, because elements alone can't carry it.
   - Only elements are shared. Then everyone's page list could differ, and that contradicts #149's user scenario.
2. **Can each person be on a different page at once?** "Independently editable" in the Summary suggests yes **(lean)**.
   - Yes means you can edit a page you aren't looking at, and your copy of it (and its thumbnail) updates in the background as peers edit it.
   - No ("everyone follows the host") is much simpler, but it goes against the Summary.
3. **Which per-page settings are shared, and which stay personal?**
   - My lean: **scroll and zoom stay personal**. They're the viewport, and upstream Excalidraw never syncs them.
   - **Background colour and grid** could go either way. Upstream doesn't sync appState at all.
   - **`showThumbnail`** feels like a personal preference.
   - Whatever you choose here becomes an AC.
4. **Should page order and folders (#162) sync?**
   - Syncing them adds a "last change wins" conflict on the whole page list.
   - Leaving them out keeps it medium, but then two people's page lists can be ordered differently.
   - My lean: **sync the order, and leave folders out of scope.**

### B. Approach: candidates for the design decision (D3 needs 2+ alternatives)

5. **How does each element know which page it's on?**
   - **(a) Tag each element with its page id** (in `customData`, the same way your creator stamp works) and keep one element stream **(lean)**. This reuses the existing reconcile, broadcast, and Firebase code almost unchanged. Every client receives every page's elements and splits them into pages locally.
   - **(b) Separate messages per page** (a new WS subtype carrying `pageId`). The protocol is cleaner, but it means rewriting reconcile and the Firebase save path. Probably too big for a medium.
   - **(c) Send the whole `pages` structure** the way file save does. This is simple, but it bypasses per-element reconcile, so two people editing at once overwrite each other.
6. **Should pages persist in the room's stored scene (Firebase)?** The stored document would gain a page-metadata field.
   - With it, someone who joins or reloads later gets all pages even when nobody else is online **(lean)**.
   - Without it, pages exist only while someone is connected.
   - Is it acceptable to change the Firebase document format?

### C. Starting and joining

7. **What happens when you start a session from a multi-page drawing?** All pages go into the room **(lean)**.
8. **What happens to your own pages when you join someone else's room?** They're replaced by the room's pages, the same way upstream already replaces your scene **(lean)**. That means your local pages are gone from the editor; they're only kept if you saved a file first. Should joining warn you, or is that out of scope?
9. **Rooms or clients without page data** (old rooms, or a teammate on an older build): everything lands on one page.
   - Is mixed-version support in scope? My lean: **no, leave it to #166 (backward compatibility).** #167 only guarantees that a room with no page data opens as one page.

### D. Conflicts (#149's open questions and the instructor's "conflicts" requirement)

10. **Someone deletes the page another user is on.** What happens to the person on it?
    - **(a)** They're moved by #158's rule (closest page before it), with a toast like "Page X was deleted by Y" **(lean)**.
    - **(b)** Deletion is blocked while anyone is on the page.
    - **(c)** The page stays for them until they leave it.
    - What (a) means: anything they were in the middle of drawing is lost, and their undo history is cleared.
11. **B is drawing on a page while A deletes it.** B's edits arrive after the delete.
    - The delete wins and late edits are dropped **(lean)**, or the late edits bring the page back.
    - Should A's confirmation dialog warn "2 collaborators are on this page"? That would be a new AC.
12. **Name collisions.** Two users each create a page at the same moment, and both get "Page 3". Or two users pick the same name. #160 requires unique names.
    - **(a)** Whichever arrives later is renamed to the next free name **(lean)**.
    - **(b)** Duplicates are allowed while collaborating.
    - Choosing (a) means a user's chosen name can change without them doing anything.
13. **Two users rename the same page, or reorder at the same time.** The last change wins **(lean)**. One person's change is silently overwritten. Is that acceptable?
14. **Clearing (#159) has to change.** Clearing pages you aren't on sets `elements: []`. In a room that won't spread: peers keep the elements and send them back.
    - So #167 would change `clearPages` (and "Clear canvas and all pages") to mark elements as deleted instead. That's an edit to merged #159 code. Is it in scope?

### E. Seeing collaborators (#149: "What do users see of collaborators on other pages?")

15. **Cursors and selections from someone on another page.** Today they'd be drawn at their coordinates on _your_ page, which is wrong.
    - Hiding them **(lean)** is required for correctness, so I'd make it an AC.
16. **Should the page tabs show who's where**, for example avatars or "2 here" on each tab?
    - Showing presence is nice, and it helps with the conflicts in D. It adds UI work.
    - My lean: **in scope, kept simple** (count or avatars only).
17. **Follow mode.** If you're following someone and they switch pages, do you switch with them?
    - Yes is natural, but it adds work.
    - My lean: **out of scope.**

### F. Permissions, your visibility features, and undo

18. **Permissions.** View-mode users can still move between pages on their own, but can't create, rename, delete, or reorder them, extending #158's rule. Real roles are out of scope; that's your admin idea for later. **(lean)** Agree?
19. **Hidden collaborators (#80–#83).** If you hide user X, X's elements are hidden on _every_ page, including thumbnails **(lean)**.
    - This means thumbnails must use `getLocallyVisibleElements`, and they may not today.
20. **Undo.** Out of scope: #168 owns it. The only behavior #167 defines is that a remote delete of your page clears your history, same as switching pages. Agree?

### G. Scope, performance, testing

21. **Performance.** Every client holds all pages, and the periodic full resync sends every page.
    - The Firebase size limit (`collabSaveFailed_sizeExceeded`) now counts all pages together, so a big multi-page drawing could hit it sooner.
    - Accept this and note it as tech debt **(lean)**, or set a page cap?
22. **Medium scope.** My proposed **in-scope list**:

    - elements tagged and synced by page
    - shared page list, names, and order
    - independent navigation
    - pages persisted in the room
    - delete/rename/name-collision conflicts
    - hiding off-page cursors, plus simple presence on tabs
    - fixing clearing so it syncs

    **Out of scope:**

    - folders
    - follow mode
    - mixed versions (#166)
    - undo (#168)
    - roles
    - performance work

    Is that a medium to you, or should we cut presence or room persistence?

23. **Testing.** Testing two real clients automatically is hard in this repo.
    - Acceptable plan **(lean)**: unit-test the pure logic (splitting elements by page, merging page metadata, resolving conflicts), integration-test `App` with simulated remote updates, and do a documented manual test with two browsers against the local `excalidraw-room`, recorded in Test Evidence. OK?

Answer by number. "Agree" works where you're fine with my lean. When I draft, the dependencies will list #157, #165, plus #158, #159, #160, and #162, since #167 has to work with all of them.

If you want to keep this work, I can move this session to a folder you choose.

# CLAUDE.md

## Project Structure

Excalidraw is a **monorepo** with a clear separation between the core library and the application:

- **`packages/excalidraw/`** - Main React component library published to npm as `@excalidraw/excalidraw`
- **`excalidraw-app/`** - Full-featured web application (excalidraw.com) that uses the library
- **`packages/`** - Core packages: `@excalidraw/common`, `@excalidraw/element`, `@excalidraw/math`, `@excalidraw/utils`
- **`examples/`** - Integration examples (NextJS, browser script)

## Development Workflow

1. **Package Development**: Work in `packages/*` for editor features
2. **App Development**: Work in `excalidraw-app/` for app-specific features
3. **Testing**: Always run `yarn test:update` before committing
4. **Type Safety**: Use `yarn test:typecheck` to verify TypeScript

## Development Commands

```bash
yarn test:typecheck  # TypeScript type checking
yarn test:update     # Run all tests (with snapshot updates)
yarn fix             # Auto-fix formatting and linting issues
```

## Architecture Notes

### Package System

- Uses Yarn workspaces for monorepo management
- Internal packages use path aliases (see `vitest.config.mts`)
- Build system uses esbuild for packages, Vite for the app
- TypeScript throughout with strict configuration

Closes #80 (Sub-issue)

## What changed

Implemented local client-side visibility controls for collaborators' drawings, ensuring users can independently show or hide individual, all, or none of their peers' drawings without affecting shared scene data, sync status, or other clients' views.

### Ownership & Identity (`excalidraw-app`)
- Implemented a one-time `customData.creatorId` stamp applied by the client that first introduces an element to the room (ensuring edits never transfer ownership, and pastes or duplicates belong to the paster).
- Added a robust per-tab client ID system utilizing a `localStorage` pool, Web Locks, and `sessionStorage` to allow reopened tabs to correctly reclaim their ID.
- Introduced non-volatile `USER_IDENTITY` messaging on join, new-user creation, and renames, with optional `clientId` support added to pointer and idle payloads while maintaining compatibility with older clients.
- Implemented a locally persisted, per-room "previously seen" collaborator directory.

### Editor & UI Architecture (`packages`)
- Extended `AppState` with `hiddenCollaboratorIds`, `collaboratorDirectory`, and `viewModeBeforeSelfHide` (configured to never be persisted, exported, or synced).
- Established a single centralized visibility rule (`element/ownership.ts`) consumed across rendering, hit-testing, selection/binding chokepoints, the eraser tool, search, and exports.
- Configured hidden elements so they cannot be selected, erased, bound to, or exported (while preserving existing bindings), routing never-seen creators and untagged elements into a shared miscellaneous bucket.
- Added toggle, show-all, and hide-all actions, including automatically locking view mode with an explanatory banner when a user hides their own drawings.
- Created the collaborator visibility dropdown menu positioned next to the avatars for both desktop and mobile views.

## Why

Collaborative sessions can quickly become visually cluttered, making it difficult for users to focus on specific work streams or review individual contributions. Providing client-side visibility controls allows users to filter what they see locally without disrupting the shared state, modifying real-time sync, or interfering with what other collaborators view on their own screens.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** Added an extra redundant guard at the selection and deletion chokepoints that explicitly validates collaborator visibility before applying destructive scene operations. While strictly redundant with the internal state checks in `element/ownership.ts`, this additional failsafe intentionally compromises pure architectural separation to guarantee that hidden peer elements can never be accidentally selected, mutated, or permanently erased during bulk operations. This can be removed in the future if internal safe-guards are considered enough, or until architectural design is modifie

**Encountered:** None. Implementation of this was built from scratch. Because of this, no test cases existed and had to be made.

## Notes

- Added 129 comprehensive feature tests covering multi-client collaboration flows through the real Collab/Portal, complete with control cases and mutation checks.
- All existing tests pass, and typecheck, lint, and Prettier checks are clean.

## Review
